title: Cyber Protection Brigade (CPB) Barracks Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)
references: AR 420-1, Army Facilities Management, 12 February 2008 (RAR 24 August 2012)
AR 600-20, Army Command Policy, dated 06 February 2025
AR 420-5, Army Fire and Emergency Services, 01 August 2024

Garrison Commander's Policy Letter #09 - Authorization for Unaccompanied Personnel or Single Soldiers to Reside Off-Post - CNAs, SNAs, Pregnant Soldiers, and Army Married Couples Program, 08 October 2025

sections.heading: 2. Purpose
sections.text: To establish rules and procedures to govern command teams as they oversee the living conditions of barracks-housed Soldiers.

sections.heading: 3. Intent
sections.text: To provide a safe, comfortable, and professional living environment for all service members assigned, attached, or permitted to reside in the CPB footprint.

sections.heading: 4. Applicability and Enforcement
sections.text: This policy applies to all units and personnel assigned or attached to the CPB and to all personnel who visit facilities under the control of this brigade. Portions of this policy are punitive in nature and personnel who fail to comply are subject to punishment under the UCMJ, as well as adverse administrative action or other adverse action authorized by applicable laws or regulations. Personnel not subject to the UCMJ who fail to comply may be subject to adverse administrative sanctions, including but not limited to, revocation of privileges as authorized by applicable law and regulation.

children.heading: a. Company Commander
items: Responsible for the overall good order, discipline, health, safety, security, welfare, and quality of life for all Soldiers residing in the barracks and for the serviceability of the structure.
Responsible for providing an appropriate degree of privacy that not only enhances Soldier morale, but also contributes to effectively preserving unit readiness through good order and discipline.

Counsel newly assigned personnel on the barracks visitation policy and provide them with a written copy of the barracks SOP; this task may be delegated to the first-line supervisor (FLL) who will include an explanation of the policy during the reception and integration counseling.
Post the barracks SOP on unit and barracks bulletin boards.
Periodically (not less than quarterly) confirm the accuracy of their Company's Barracks Utilization Report (BUR).

Appoint in writing, as an additional duty, a Barracks Manager (one Primary and one Alternate) to oversee the cleanliness and serviceability of all common areas in the barracks, to submit and track work/service orders, and to oversee the good order, discipline, safety, and security of the barracks daily.

children.heading: b. First Sergeant
items: Assign rooms and clear rooms in their respective areas for all incoming/outgoing personnel, to include personnel moving rooms within the CPB barracks footprint, via the program of record, Enterprise Military Housing (eMH), and ensure it is accurate NLT the last duty day of every month.
Maintain eMH and Army Maintenance (ArMA) accounts for tracking and managing barracks utilization and maintenance.
Responsible for the oversight of the assigned building's Key Control and/or Code Program.
Responsible for coordinating with the RAPTOR First Sergeant regarding the assignment of available rooms for all incoming CPB personnel.
Ensure Sexual Harassment/Assault Response & Prevention (SHARP) policies and bulletins are prominently posted, displaying contact numbers and reporting procedures.
Counsel Barracks Managers, in writing (on DA Form 4856), on their duties and responsibilities.
Conduct inspections of barracks rooms to enforce this SOP and to ensure a healthy, safe, and secure living environment allowing for, and contributing to, good order, discipline, and morale.
Perform duties as the Commander's delegated authority in executing unit policies; assist the Commander in the execution of his/her duties and responsibilities with regards to enforcement of this SOP.

children.heading: c. Platoon Sergeants / Team NCOIC / First-Line Supervisors (FLL)
items: Conduct formal and informal walk-through of their barracks rooms and common areas on a weekly basis including the weekends at random times.
Enforce this policy and further ensure a healthy, safe, and secure living environment allowing for, and contributing to, good order, discipline, and morale.

Coordinate with the Barracks Managers to execute move-out inspections to ensure Soldiers' rooms are thoroughly cleaned prior to being cleared. Upon verification of cleanliness, the Barracks Manager will notify the First Sergeant for final inspection and eMH clearance.
Ensure every resident receives, or a posted copy of this barracks SOP is on the inside portion of their room door.
Ensure the Soldier residing in the barracks has downloaded the ArMA Application and fully understands its purpose of use.

Note problems with a Soldier's room and ensure a work request to repair the deficiencies is submitted; the FLL is then responsible for following up on work order status and repairs until they are corrected.
Validate and maintain the high value inventory record (DA Form 4986) in the Soldier's counseling packet or personnel file in the company. Update at minimum every 6 months.

children.heading: d. Barracks Manager
items: Barracks Managers will be appointed, in writing, by the Company Commander on Additional Duty orders that will remain in effect until relieved or removed from those duties by the Commander.

Ensure each Soldier signs a hand receipt for the property in their assigned room; explain, and ensure the Soldier understands they assume responsibility for the ACCOUNTABILITY and SERVICEABILITY of this property upon issuance of the room.
Out-process Soldiers from the barracks through proper coordination with the Platoon Sergeants/Team NCOICs/FLL, and the First Sergeant.

Inspect rooms of departing Soldiers to ensure cleanliness, property accountability, and property serviceability; report any rooms that are improperly cleaned or maintained to the First Sergeant. The Barracks Manager WILL NOT sign or stamp the Soldier as "Cleared" on their clearing papers -- only the First Sergeant that owns the building may do that, on the clearing papers and in eMH.
Responsible for the accuracy of the Barracks Utilization Report.
Ensure the Soldier completes and submits a list of damage/deficiencies found in their room.

Organize and supervise cleaning parties to accomplish large scale cleaning jobs; has authority over residents in areas pertaining to the overall maintenance of the barracks and the good order and discipline within the barracks.

Assist the Brigade Safety Officer and NCO in ensuring Fire and Emergency Evacuation Plans are current, posted, and practiced; coordinate to conduct fire drills and correct safety issues; ensure all safety equipment (e.g., fire extinguishers) are inspected and serviceable.
Ensure no hazardous materials (HAZMAT) are stored within the barracks and that Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) are current and on hand for cleaning supplies.
Ensure enough cleaning supplies and tools are available for cleaning details to efficiently execute their tasks.
Attend U-Do-It training and use the garrison U-Do-It facility to acquire items for residents that DPW does not provide.
Ensure name placards are current and posted (see the Building/Unit reference below).
Assign Floor Managers who will monitor issues within the barracks to ensure this policy is followed.

children.heading: e. Floor Manager
items: Responsible for creating and maintaining the daily cleaning roster.
Responsible for reporting any cleanliness issues or anything unusual to the Barracks Manager, or to the Staff Duty Officer if the situation is egregious enough.
Attend U-Do-It training and use the garrison U-Do-It facility to acquire items for residents that DPW does not provide.

children.heading: f. Soldier
items: Responsible for reading, understanding, and maintaining the standards in this SOP.
Assist in the maintenance of common areas of the building they reside in, regardless of the company or battalion they are a part of.
Optional: attend U-Do-It training to acquire items for immediate resolution in their assigned room.

children.heading: a. Room Standards
items: Soldiers may arrange and decorate their rooms within the limits of good taste. Nothing will be displayed that is inappropriate (e.g., nudity, pro-drug messages, extremist symbols, extreme cruelty, or values incompatible with normal unit cohesion). Non-government furniture, telephones, civilian blankets, and other comforts are allowed -- address any questions of suitability to the First Sergeant.

Personally owned furniture will not interfere with another Soldier's allocated space and must be kept clean, neat, and in good repair, or removed. Government furniture not meeting these conditions will be reported to the Barracks Manager and removed. Each resident signs a hand receipt for the furniture they're responsible for maintaining in their room.
Furnishings will be neatly arranged and kept free of clutter and dust.
Furnishings will not restrict any egress route to less than three feet in width.
Moving government furniture from one room to another is not authorized.

children.heading: b. Maintenance
items: All work order requests will be submitted through ArMA. Mold-related work order requests must be accompanied with pictures, or they will not be actioned.
Contact the Floor Manager or Barracks Manager for replacement of unserviceable furnishings or items.

children.heading: c. Common Area Standards
items: Dayrooms/game rooms will be clean and organized; trash cans emptied and recreation equipment neatly stored.

Laundry area floors will be swept and mopped regularly. Dryer lint traps cleaned immediately after use; washers and dryers cleaned inside and out; sinks (if present) wiped out and free of debris; countertops wiped down and dried. Personal items left unattended in laundry rooms for more than 24 hours will be secured by the Barracks Manager and turned over to the Supply Sergeant, held for a maximum of 48 hours before disposal. CTA-50 or field gear of any type will NOT be placed in a washer or dryer -- unattended CTA-50 items will be secured and turned over to the First Sergeant. Soldiers may be charged for any damage to washers/dryers from washing unauthorized items, and for any damage to the CTA-50 itself.
Windows will be cleaned if necessary.
Grill areas will be cleaned -- no charcoal debris, surfaces cleaned, all trash removed.

Area beautification and lawn maintenance: all debris removed and grass/weeds cut around the building, including the parking area (and, where applicable, the street or the next unit's assigned area such as a sidewalk).

children.heading: d. Visitation
items: Visitors will NOT be allowed to stay in the barracks room while the resident is absent.
Overnight visitors are NOT authorized at any time.
Visiting hours are 0600-2300 on weekdays and 0600-0200 on weekends and holidays. NO EXCEPTIONS.

Per AR 420-1, you are negligent if you're aware that a visitor you allow on the premises is likely to act recklessly and you don't take proper steps to prevent or minimize it -- and grossly negligent if you know damage is likely and fail to act, in which case you'll be charged for the full amount of the loss.
Cohabitation in the barracks is strictly PROHIBITED. This includes overnight stays and sleepovers.
At no time will an Officer visit enlisted barracks except for official business, and no inspection (formal, informal, or health & welfare) will take place unaccompanied by an NCO or Officer.
No visitors under the age of 18 are allowed at any time. If minors are found in the barracks, the MPs will be called to remove the minor and the Soldier's chain of command will be notified.

children.heading: e. Quiet Hours
items: Quiet hours are in effect from 2200 to 0600, every day, in all CPB barracks.

Keep the volume of radios, stereos, televisions, etc. low enough that it doesn't disturb adjacent rooms or areas -- if it can be heard through the walls or from outside the room's entrance, it's too loud.
The same applies to noise from outside gatherings near the barracks. Violators will be warned once; a subsequent occurrence gets reported to the appropriate First Sergeant.

Habitual violators can have the privilege of using such systems suspended by the Company Commander. Remember that some CPB personnel are shift workers, so be considerate. Personal property will not be seized except in relation to an imminent safety concern, to prevent a crime, or to safeguard evidence of a crime -- and only with a Commander's order citing specific facts and circumstances.

children.heading: 1. Prohibited in the barracks
items: Smoking -- prohibited in any stairwell, within 50 feet of any building, and within individual rooms.
Candles, incense, fireworks, and any other item that requires or contains an open flame.
Hotplates, grills, and any electric cookery, unless approved in writing by the Fort Gordon Fire Department.
Flammable or combustible items (e.g., lighter fluid for cooking grills) -- residents may have ONE 12 oz. container of cigarette lighter fluid.
Space heaters.

children.heading: 2. Safe evacuation procedures
items: Three feet of clearance is required for all egress routes.
Grills of any kind on patios or in stairways are prohibited.
Bicycles or other property will not be stored in exit pathways or stairwells.
Bicycles will be marked to identify owner and unit.

children.heading: 3-6. General fire safety
items: Smoke only in designated areas; not within 50 feet of fuel storage tanks or paint lockers. Dispose of cigarette butts in approved containers only.
DO NOT tamper with smoke alarms, fire extinguishers, or any safety device -- it jeopardizes everyone's safety.

When a fire is discovered: give a vocal alarm, pull the fire alarm, call 911, evacuate and assemble at the designated area, and notify the Barracks Manager. The senior person on site takes a headcount; anyone unaccounted for (residents or visitors) is reported to the First Sergeant. A Soldier is posted near the roadway to guide emergency responders. DO NOT reenter the building until an "All Clear" is issued by the Fire Department or Military Police.

If the fire is small, attempt to put it out with the closest fire extinguisher and still notify the Barracks Manager and the Fort Gordon Fire Department. Fire extinguisher points are clearly marked and easily accessible.

children.heading: g. Crime Prevention, Physical Security, and Safety
items: Rooms will ALWAYS be locked. Stolen/vandalized items may not be replaced or reimbursed if lost to negligence (failure to properly secure them) -- the installation Claims Office determines if a claim is cognizable.

Prescription medication, money, security badges, and other items of value (bank/credit cards, checkbooks, postage stamps, etc.) must be physically secured when the room is unoccupied. An unlocked desk or dresser drawer does not satisfy this requirement.

An inventory record (DA Form 4986) will be completed for personal property of high value and updated at minimum every six months. The military may not replace/reimburse stolen or vandalized items if ownership can't be proven.

NCOs residing in the barracks handle minor problems; anything that can't be handled is reported immediately to the FLL, and if needed escalated higher and/or to the First Sergeant. All numbers are on the alert roster.
Storage of combustible materials within the barracks is prohibited.
Soldiers are encouraged not to keep large amounts of cash or irreplaceable high-value items in their room -- coordinate temporary storage with the unit supply NCO or S4.

children.heading: h. Weapons
children.text: NO weapons of any type are allowed in the barracks -- including firearms, BB/pellet guns, knives with blades over three inches, switchblades, butterfly knives, martial arts weapons, axes, hatchets, crossbows, bows and arrows, and blowguns. Firearms and other similarly lethal weapons are stored in the arms room. All other weapons are stored in a wall locker in the unit supply room.

children.heading: i. Alcohol/Drugs
items: Alcohol may be consumed in barracks rooms, day rooms, and picnic areas only -- not in hallways, latrines, or outside designated picnic areas. Police up after yourself in dayrooms. Keg beer is not authorized. Limit per room at any one time: one 12-pack (144 oz.) of beer, OR two 750 ml bottles of wine, OR one 750 ml bottle of liquor. Providing alcohol to anyone prohibited from consuming/possessing/receiving it is prohibited.

Prescription medications will be disposed of by their expiration date, or once the prescribed quantity is used up. Do not share prescription medication or participate in illegal drug use in any manner. All CPB personnel are eligible for random urinalysis IAW Army and local policy.

children.heading: j. Pets
children.text: NO PETS ARE AUTHORIZED in CPB barracks.

children.heading: a. PII disposal
children.text: There will be ABSOLUTELY NO PII or sensitive items thrown in the dumpsters.

children.heading: b. Inspections
items: Informal "walk-through" inspections check that barracks standards are met and there are no health/safety hazards. These are unannounced and may happen on duty or non-duty days.
Residents are subject to unannounced Health and Welfare Inspections at the Commander's discretion.

Damage beyond "fair wear and tear" results in a Statement of Charges for repair/replacement cost. Upon assignment to a room, residents have 72 hours to prepare a list of existing damage or deficiencies.

children.heading: c. Clearing
items: Soldiers moving out must thoroughly clean their assigned room before being signed off as "Cleared" by the Barracks Manager and/or First Sergeant.

Upon notification of PCS or ETS, Soldiers must give their First Sergeant a minimum of two weeks' notice with a final clearing date. If the Soldier's building is owned by a different company, that company's First Sergeant must be notified no later than 72 hours from notification. Exception: Soldiers who promote to Staff Sergeant, or who have a change in dependency status (with official documentation), are allotted 30 calendar days from that date instead of two weeks' notice.
At final inspection, only items on the hand receipt should remain in the room. Refrigerators are turned to the minimum cool setting -- do not unplug or turn them off.

children.heading: d. Energy Conservation
children.text: Residents will turn off all electrical devices (TVs, DVD players, computers, printers, etc.) and room lights when not present, and close and lock windows when not present.

children.heading: e. Customs and Courtesies
children.text: Residents will execute proper customs and courtesies -- calling "Attention" or "At Ease" when a superior Officer or NCO enters or leaves your room. Because of 24/7 quiet hours in CPB barracks, Soldiers will not call "Attention" or "At Ease" on the floor or in common areas.

children.heading: f. Complaints or Ideas for Improvement
children.text: Soldiers with complaints or ideas for improving quality of life in the barracks are encouraged to inform their Chain of Command, or to involve the B.O.S.S. Council through their unit's B.O.S.S. representative.

sections.heading: 8. Point of Contact
sections.text: Questions about this SOP should be directed to your Barracks Manager, Floor Manager, or First Sergeant.

sections.heading: Annex A -- Off-Post Housing Policy (Garrison Commander's Policy #09)
sections.text: Covers when single Soldiers may live off-post instead of in the barracks. Full policy letter dated 8 October 2025.

children.heading: Who this applies to
children.text: Applies only to single Soldiers in the rank of SGT or below. These Soldiers are required to reside in the barracks unless a Certificate of Non-Availability (CNA), Exception to Policy (ETP), or other authorization permits them to live off-post. SSG and above are automatically entitled to BAH. Unit commanders may not authorize Soldiers to reside off-post -- approval authority is delegated to the Fort Gordon Unaccompanied Housing (UH) Manager, with appeal to the Garrison Commander.

children.heading: Certificate of Non-Availability (CNA)
children.text: Permanent party Soldiers are issued a CNA when installation Single Soldier Housing (SSH) exceeds the required 95% occupancy rate (per AR 420-1). Brigade-level unit integrity is maintained where possible, but Soldiers may be assigned outside their Brigade footprint. Soldiers may not sign a binding lease until they receive approved documentation -- doing so early is at their own risk, does not guarantee BAH or back pay, and having pets, storage fees, or household goods does not justify approval to live off-post.

children.heading: Exceptions to Policy (ETP)
children.text: Handled case-by-case through the government housing office. Requests need, at minimum, a written request with the Soldier's Brigade Commander's endorsement plus supporting documents.
items: Medical exceptions: submitted on a Personnel Action Request or DA 4187-1-R with supporting medical documentation, processed through the chain of command to Brigade level, then to the Housing Office. Approval is based on the Preventive Health OIC's medical recommendation.

Soldiers married to non-military spouses: a Soldier with no other dependents who is granted a divorce may be issued a CNA through the end of their current lease (lease must have been in effect 91+ days before the divorce decree). Not extended beyond the current 12-month lease; the Soldier then moves into SSH, without an authorized government move back on post (excess household goods stored at government expense).

Pregnant Soldiers: authorized to reside off-post after the 20th week of pregnancy (per licensed medical authority), via a Personnel Action Request or DA 4187 with medical documentation and expected due date. BAH starts at the without-dependent rate through the Fort Gordon Finance Office; a birth certificate copy is required afterward to move to the with-dependent rate. The Housing Service Office (Suite 129, Darling Hall) can help locate and negotiate an off-post lease. Pregnant Soldiers may also be waitlisted for on-post Family housing. Any change in dependency status (e.g., loss of the expected child) must be reported immediately to the Housing Office, Finance Office, and the housing operator, and requires a return to SSH.

Army Married Couple Program: Soldiers married to Soldiers with no dependents, both assigned to Fort Gordon or within a 1-hour commute, may reside off-post (or in on-post Family housing) at the without-dependent BAH rate each. If a Joint Domicile CNA doesn't apply (orders to the same installation within 120 days of each other), a CNA isn't required to reside off-post -- but each Soldier must submit a DA Form 5960, a copy of the marriage license, and a copy of both sets of orders.

Geographic Bachelors: Permanent Party Soldiers entitled to with-dependent BAH are not authorized SSH assignment and will not reside in SSH on Fort Gordon (this doesn't include Soldiers on TCS/TDY orders).

Homeowners: Soldiers who purchased a home near the installation before their Fort Gordon assignment was announced are authorized to reside off-post, with closing documentation attached to a Personnel Action Request or DA 4187, approved by the Housing Office.

Soldiers supporting Family members: Soldiers required to pay BAH for Family member support due to divorce/separation, or with other legally supported dependents (e.g., children or parents), are not required to occupy SSH or obtain a CNA -- supporting documentation goes to the Fort Gordon Finance Office.

children.heading: Submitting a CNA request
children.text: The Garrison UH Housing Manager reviews all CNA requests before forwarding them to the Garrison Commander for consideration. Requests include: a Personnel Action Request or DA 4187 detailing the reason and endorsed by the Battalion Commander (an ETP CNA must be endorsed by the Brigade Commander); orders assigning the Service Member to Fort Gordon; and supporting documents (lease, marriage certificate, divorce certificate, etc.). Statements of Non-Availability (SNA) are processed the same way through the Fort Gordon Housing Office, approved/disapproved by the UH Housing Manager.

sections.heading: Annex C -- Standard Room Hand-Receipt Items
sections.text: The blank hand-receipt template used to inventory government furniture issued with each room (Barcode, Serial Number, Condition, and Purchase Cost are filled in per Soldier at move-in). Standard items listed: pedestal study-carrel desk, single mattress/boxspring (36"x80"), chest of drawers, right pedestal desk, microfridge refrigerator, ergonomic desk chair, and a stackable single bunk with metal panels.
